BAGONG PIUP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City OPINION NO. FEB 1 3 2025 ATTY. HARVEY ECKER A. ZAMORA Secretary to the Sangguniang Panlungsod Office of the Sangguniang Panlungsod City of Calapan, Province of Oriental Mindoro Dear Atty. Zamora: This has reference to your letter dated 18 October 2024 seeking this Department's legal opinion regarding the adoption of technology-based betting system by cockpit operators in the City of Calapan. Per the letter, the SP of Calapan City enacted City Ordinance No. 96, Series of 2021 and City Ordinance No. 95, Series of 2021, granting two separate franchises for two cockpit operators in Calapan City. You represented that the franchisees were required, per National IATF on COVID 19 to install technology-based betting machines manned by tellers inside their respective cockpits. You then stated that installation of these betting machines proved to be convenient and simplified the betting and collection of winnings in the cockpit. You alleged that you were aware that the issuances by the National IATF on COVID- 19 have been revoked. However, you stated that data indicates that the same technology-based betting machines manned by tellers have been continuously used by cockpit operators in other municipalities. Perusal of the letter reveals that you are seeking guidance and legal opinion on the following matters: 1. Whether or not the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Calapan can legally amend the City Ordinance to allow the use of technology-based betting machines manned by tellers and installed with the cockpit premises during their regular and special cockfights? 2. Whether or not cockpit operators can continue to use technology-based betting machines manned by tellers and installed within the cockpit premises during their regular and special cockfights in the absence of that provision in their franchise? "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

3. Whether or not the use of technology-based betting machines manned by tellers and installed within the cockpit premises during their regular and special cockfights is legal despite the fact that there is no longer a State of National Health Emergency? Thus, the request for guidance and legal opinion. At the outset, we are of the assumption that "technology-based betting machines" refer to machines used for physical placement of bets situated within traditional cockpits, and not accessible to bettors situated outside the cockpits. The Sangguniang Panlungsod is authorized under Sec. 458(a)(3)(v) of the Local Government Code to regulate cockfighting.l We are of the view that the authority to regulate necessarily includes the amendment of the existing City Ordinance to allow the use of technology-based betting machines. While "technology-based betting machines" installed in the cockpit premises may appear to be covered by the term "all-betting plafforms that may be situated inside the cockpit" mentioned in Section 12 of Executive Order No. 09, dated December 8, 2022, this is qualified by the phrase "any of the following activities relating to E-Sabon$. Moreover, Section I likewise states that "The operations of traditional cockfights authorized or licensed under existing laws shall not be covered by the foregoing suspension." Thus, the Department opines that the use of technology-based betting machines is prohibited only if such is related to E-Sabong. Cockpit operators may continue to use technology-based betting machines installed within cockpit premises as long as this is not expressly prohibited3 in their franchise and its operation is not accessible to 1 (v) Any law to the contrary notwithstanding, authorize and license the establishment, operation, and maintenance of cockpits, and regulate cockfighting and commercial breeding of gamecocks: Provided, That existing rights should not be prejudiced; 2 Section 1. Continued Suspension of E-Sabong Operations. All E-Sabong operations, including all auxiliary E-Sabong operations and off cockpit betting station operations, shall continue to be suspended nationwide. Consistent with the Regulatory Framework for E-Sabong, ESAO, and OCBS issued by the PAGCOR, and relevant laws, rules and regulations, anv of the followinq activities relatinq to E-Sabonq is suspended: a. Live-streaming or broadcasting of live-cockfights outside cockpits or cockfighting arenas or premises where cockfights are being held; and/or b. Online/remote or off-cockpit wagering/betting on live cockfighting matches, events and/or activities streamed or broadcasted live, regardless of the location of the betting platform, including but not limited to all bettinq platforms that may be situated inside the cockpit or cockfiqhtinq arenas, or premises where cockfights are held. The operations of traditional cockfiqhts authorized or licensed under existinq laws shall not be covered bv the foreqoinq suspension. 3 It is a rule of statutory construction that what is not expressly or impliedly prohibited by law may be done, except when the act is contrary to morals, customs and public order. (Manila Electric Company vs. Public Service Commission, G.R. No. 42317, September 21, 1934. Page 2 of 3

bettors situated outside the cockpits. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P.
